newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine main opposition parties closing ranks.
newsitem.headline: Argentine main opposition parties closing ranks.

text.p: Argentina's two leading opposition parties moved a step closer on Monday towards forging an alliance against President Carlos Menem's ruling Peronists.

"We'll have to chart common strategies to face greater challenges in the near future," former President Raul Alfonsin of the Radical Party told reporters after meeting Frepaso leader Carlos "Chacho" Alvarez.
Alvarez was bolder, saying the parties hoped to run together in some districts in next year's midterm elections.
"It would be good if in 1997 we have joint slates (of candidates) in as many districts as possible," said Alvarez.
Those elections were seen as a measure of Menem's popularity, which is at an all-time low in the aftermath of a year-long recession.

Labour unions, once fiercely loyal to the government, have held two major strikes in the past two months and are threatening more action against austerity policies. On both occasions they were supported by the Radicals and the Frepaso.
"Since we're not chosing a government in 1997, what we need to do is get a majority in the Lower House of Congress that will vote together," said Alfonsin.
The centrist Radicals were relegated to a humiliating third place behind newcomers Frepaso, a coalition of leftists and disenchanted Peronists, in 1995 general elections.
The polls were swept by Menem, who clinched re-lection with 50 percent of the vote.

However the Radicals, taking advantage their traditional power base in Buenos Aires, bounced back with a resounding victory in the city's first-every mayora elections last June. Frepaso came second and the Peronists trailed third.
